tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Outcome analytics: the application funnel plus breakdowns by career track, domain, country, visa verdict and match band, and rejection statistics. Groups below the sample threshold are flagged as low-confidence.

tools.name: get_application
tools.description: One application's full history: every status transition with its source (user, email or pipeline), and any rejection analysis. Rejection analysis keeps the employer's stated reason strictly apart from our hypotheses.

tools.name: get_ats_report
tools.description: ATS scoring for a job against the user's current resume: eight component scores, the highest-value keywords absent from the resume, and concrete suggestions. Keywords are derived from that specific posting, so this works the same for any industry.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Full detail for one job: classification, required and preferred skills, ATS keywords, the work-authorization verdict with the exact posting phrases behind it, and why it ranks where it does. Includes a description excerpt so you can read the posting's own wording.

tools.name: get_learning_signals
tools.description: The career learning loop's current findings: recurring skill gaps across targeted jobs, certifications the postings keep asking for, which track is converting, and whether the resume rather than the fit is the problem.

tools.name: get_match_detail
tools.description: Per-requirement breakdown of how the user matches one job: which requirements are directly evidenced, which are partially or only transferably covered, which are outright gaps, and the evidence ids behind each. The `claimable` flag tells you what a resume may assert.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: The user's Master Profile: experience, location and mobility, work authorization per country, credentials, and their parallel career tracks. Read this before giving any strategic advice.

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: The application pipeline across all lifecycle states, optionally filtered by status.

tools.name: list_email_messages
tools.description: Classified job-related email with the fields extracted from each message (company, position, interview time, assessment deadline, required action). Filter by category or by whether the message needs action.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: List discovered jobs in ranked order (deadline tier first, then priority score). Use this to orient before drilling into specific jobs. Filter by country code, career domain id, or deadline bucket (today | within_48h | within_7d | future | none).

tools.name: search_evidence
tools.description: Search the Career Evidence Database - the atomic verified facts every resume claim must trace back to. Filter by free text or by a skill-graph id. Use this to check what the user can actually evidence before you claim anything on their behalf.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search jobs with a natural-language query, e.g. 'H1B-friendly cybersecurity jobs in Texas', 'remote data engineering in India', 'deadline today', 'match above 85%'. Returns how the query was interpreted alongside the results, so you can tell whether the filter matched your intent.

tools.name: add_application_note
tools.description: Append a note to an application - context worth keeping for later.

tools.name: analyze_job
tools.description: Re-run the full analysis for one job: classification, work-authorization eligibility, skill match, ATS score and priority. Use when a job looks unclassified or stale. Returns the refreshed detail.

tools.name: draft_cover_letter
tools.description: Draft a cover letter for a job using only evidence the user can actually claim for it. Requirements they cannot evidence are acknowledged as gaps rather than papered over.

tools.name: draft_email_reply
tools.description: Draft a reply to a classified job email. High-impact topics (immigration, sponsorship commitments, salary negotiation, contracts, offers, resignation, legal) are detected on both the incoming message and the generated reply; when any fires the draft is held and cannot be approved or sent. Nothing here sends mail - there is no send tool.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: Build a job-specific resume assembled from the Career Evidence Database, then run the factuality check. The check always runs and its verdict always comes back: a resume with any unsupported claim returns `is_final: false` and cannot be sent. Gaps the user cannot evidence are reported, never filled in.

tools.name: update_application_status
tools.description: Move an application to a new lifecycle status, recording the transition with source 'agent' so it is distinguishable from the user's own updates and from email-driven ones. Only do this when the user asked, or when an email clearly established the new state.

withheld_capabilities.name: add_evidence
withheld_capabilities.reason: Evidence is the user's verified truth and the sole support for every resume claim. An agent that can write evidence can manufacture the support for anything it wants to say.

withheld_capabilities.name: verify_evidence
withheld_capabilities.reason: Verification is the user asserting a fact is true. The agent cannot promote its own inputs from unverified to verified.

withheld_capabilities.name: edit_evidence
withheld_capabilities.reason: Same reason as add_evidence: the substrate is not the agent's to edit.

withheld_capabilities.name: delete_evidence
withheld_capabilities.reason: Destructive, and would let the agent hide a contradiction.

withheld_capabilities.name: set_eligibility
withheld_capabilities.reason: Work-authorization verdicts come from the country pack's rules applied to the posting's own words. They are not a model output.

withheld_capabilities.name: mark_resume_final
withheld_capabilities.reason: `is_final` is set by the factuality checker and by nothing else. It is the gate, so it cannot be a tool.

withheld_capabilities.name: set_factuality_passed
withheld_capabilities.reason: Would defeat the entire resume safety model.

withheld_capabilities.name: send_email
withheld_capabilities.reason: Phase 1 never auto-sends. Replies go DRAFT -> human approval -> send, and high-impact topics never leave draft state at all.

withheld_capabilities.name: approve_draft
withheld_capabilities.reason: Approval is the human's act; it is what the gate is for.

withheld_capabilities.name: submit_application
withheld_capabilities.reason: ASSISTED mode: CareerOS assembles the packet, the human submits. Nothing here bypasses CAPTCHA, MFA or bot protection.

withheld_capabilities.name: execute_sql
withheld_capabilities.reason: Arbitrary database access would route around every constraint above.

withheld_capabilities.name: run_shell
withheld_capabilities.reason: Not a capability a career agent needs.

agentTools.note: The agent has autonomy over strategy, not over truthfulness. The withheld capabilities do not exist as tools, so no prompt reaches them.

providers.label: Google Jobs
providers.notes:
Surfaces the boards you asked for in one query: each result carries a
`via` field naming where Google found it (LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter,
Glassdoor, Monster, CareerBuilder, Dice, or the employer directly), which
is stored as the job's board so per-board conversion analytics still work.
SerpApi has a free tier; the key is yours.

providers.label: Google Search → company career pages
providers.notes:
Google's own Programmable Search JSON API (100 queries/day free). Used to
find postings on employers' own career sites -- Workday, Taleo, iCIMS,
SuccessFactors, bespoke pages -- that never reach an aggregator. Each hit
is fetched once, robots.txt permitting, and the posting is read from the
schema.org JobPosting the page publishes for exactly this purpose.

providers.label: Adzuna
providers.notes:
Free developer key, generous limits, real coverage in both the United
States and India. The broadest single source that does not need a paid
plan.

providers.label: Jooble
providers.notes: Free API key. Aggregates boards and company sites, strong in India.

providers.label: Careerjet
providers.notes: Free affiliate key. Country coverage set by locale_code.

providers.label: USAJOBS (federal)
providers.notes:
Free key, and the only source here that reliably carries a real
application deadline -- which the priority engine ranks above score.

providers.label: The Muse
providers.notes: Works with no key at all. Curated employers, mostly US.

providers.label: Arbeitnow
providers.notes: No key. Europe-heavy, plus remote roles open worldwide.

providers.label: ZipRecruiter (partner API)
providers.notes:
Requires a ZipRecruiter publisher/partner key. Until you have one, their
listings still arrive through google_jobs, which indexes ZipRecruiter.

providers.label: CareerBuilder (partner API)
providers.notes:
Requires a CareerBuilder developer token. Their listings also arrive
through google_jobs in the meantime.

providers.label: Dice (partner API)
providers.notes:
Dice's marketplace API needs a key from their partner programme. Endpoint
and field names are per their current docs and are not verified here --
run `careeros sources check dice` once you have a key.

providers.label: Monster (partner feed)
providers.notes:
Monster serves search results as RSS per saved search. Create the search
on Monster, copy its feed URL, and set CAREEROS_MONSTER_FEEDS to a
comma-separated list. Nothing is guessed on your behalf.

providers.label: Any RSS/Atom job feed
providers.notes:
Generic feed reader for anything that publishes one: a company's careers
feed, a niche board, a saved search on a board that offers RSS. Set
CAREEROS_RSS_FEEDS to a comma-separated list of URLs.

providers.label: Greenhouse boards
providers.notes: One entry per employer board token, e.g. stripe,figma,airbnb.

providers.label: LinkedIn (direct)
providers.reason:
LinkedIn's User Agreement forbids automated collection, and job search
sits behind bot protection and an authentication wall. Getting past
either is exactly what this system will not do.
providers.partner_route: LinkedIn Talent Solutions job-posting APIs are partner-gated; if you are granted access, add it as a `rest` provider here.

providers.label: Indeed (direct)
providers.reason:
Indeed retired its open Publisher API and its terms forbid scraping
search results. It is Cloudflare-protected.
providers.partner_route: Indeed's employer/ATS integrations and its Partner programme are the sanctioned routes.

providers.label: Glassdoor (direct)
providers.reason: Glassdoor's job APIs were withdrawn and its terms forbid automated collection.

providers.label: Naukri (direct)
providers.reason:
Naukri has no public job-search API and its terms forbid automated
collection. It is the largest board in India, so this one costs you real
coverage -- Adzuna, Jooble and Google Jobs are the substitutes.
